exposure: Infection prevention bundle (pre-operative bathing, single dose of injectable cephalexin within one hour of incision, spontaneous removal of placenta)
Traditional method (injection of ceftriaxone for 48 hours followed by oral antibiotics for 5 days)
outcome: Cesarean section surgical site infection (CS-SSI) rate
cohort: The study included 184 pregnant women planned for cesarean sections, chosen by simple random sampling, with no recent infection, in a predominantly unbooked and low-income population.
finding: There was no statistically significant difference in the infection rate between the infection prevention bundle group (2.2%) and the traditional method group (1.1%) for controlling cesarean section surgical site infection.
mod_finding: The study compares different infection prevention methods for cesarean sections, which is a mode of birth.
